The lighter downloads are merged into main ([#985](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/985)); its CI checks had passed. The planner now opens on the festival overview and downloads programmes only for same-country festivals that overlap the trip.

2	name: planng-year-strip-design
3	description: Ariel's agreed design for the planNG year festival strip (popularity rows + faint background), not yet built
4	metadata:
5	  type: project
6	  modified: 2026-10-02T15:07:09.363Z
7	---
8	
9	Agreed with Ariel 2026-10-02 in the "lighter downloads" thread; mockups in /mnt/project-files/strip-groups/thin-*.png. Not implemented yet; Ariel said build only when asked.
10	
11	- No grouping by geography or festival class: those are filters (chips), and grouping by them breaks once you filter by them.
12	- Rank festivals by popularity (proxy: Google search result count; needs a per-festival number from the festival finder, which needs a search API key).
13	- Three thin rows (~12px bars). Place most popular first into the first row where it clears neighbours by a gap; skip ones that don't fit; a long festival (7+ days) goes to the fitting row holding the fewest long festivals, so long ones don't stack in the top row; stop when rows are 70% full (Ariel chose 70% over 40%).
14	- Everything else drawn behind, freely across the whole strip height, as faint, desaturated, transparent versions of their type colour.
15	- No text on the grid when crowded; names on hover. Text only when the filter leaves ~10 or fewer.
16	- Ranking and fill are recomputed inside the current filter.
17	- Changing a filter must animate: items added, removed, or promoted from background into a row (and demoted) with transitions.
18	- Hovering the strip magnifies the weeks under the cursor (macOS Dock style fisheye); names appear only on enlarged bars. Prototype: https://claude.ai/artifact/TMjQmooGEKkvipxvfWAL96
19	- Bar height is one visual requirement for all three controls, set by the globe: drop the place dropdown under the globe, drop the labels under the type tiles (hover popup: name, festival count, subtypes, next one), and give the strip as many rows as fit (9 at the tile grid's height), filled to 70% (Ariel chose 70% again with more rows). No text line under the strip. Type tiles on the left, globe on the right; both top-aligned with the first row of festivals, not the month axis.
20	- The globe looks like a physical desk globe: tan land on deep-blue sea, sphere shading with a highlight, a tilted brass meridian ring and a small wooden stand, all within the bar height (globe shrinks to ~130px).
21	
22	**Why:** pre-filter, users want where/when it's busy and which landmarks fall there; the old country-chained groups made too many groups and too much text.
23	**How to apply:** use this as the spec when the strip redesign is requested; write each bullet as a requirement leaf.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a repo: mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to adopt or set up Claudinite, or to re-vendor a repo's mount.
- adopt-pack: Add packs to a repo already running Claudinite: declare, interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable or declare a pack.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- backfilling-provenance: Filling a pack's empty provenance files from its history. Use when a pack carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill a pack's provenance.
- bug-investigation: Pinning down a bug's root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce.
- changing-pack-elements: What a change to a pack's element owes: the provenance entry, its kind, what a README carries. Loaded for any edit of a pack's rules, skills, checks, tasks or manifest.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Finding where a repo's CI time goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, on a runtime regression, or on a ci-performance finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut: one concern per commit, the issue it references, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- data-pipeline: EdFringeNow's data pipeline - getting show data out of edfringe.com into the committed files the site serves, and the wire format the pages decode. Use before touching scraper/, data/, site/data/, the scrape and price tasks, or the site code that decodes, prices or times performances.
- deterministic-expecteds: What makes a rendered expected byte-stable, and the per-stack rendering recipe. Use when writing a case, the render harness or the fake world under dev/requirements.
- do-later: File a change to be made after the work in flight, as an issue queued behind it. Use on "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or any deferred change.
- explore-link: Mine one URL for product, market, usage and pricing insights and fold them into a product-wiki page. Use on "/explore-link <url>", or when handed a link for the wiki.
- extract-from-instructions: Convert instruction prose somebody already wrote into pack carriers. Use when adopting Claudinite on a repo with a CLAUDE.md, or when asked to convert instruction prose into a pack.
- festival-finder: A festival finder run - searching for festivals with a per-session programme and growing the lists of candidates and search sources. Use when asked to find more festivals or conferences.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or file from the web: exact bytes over a summary, and what a 403 or egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl.
- file-placement: Where a file should live: the reference-distance metric and its exemptions. Use before placing, moving or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the basics task lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees. Use when adding, changing, explaining or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a technology nobody there has used yet. Use when asked to host, send or publish through something new, or to research it and create a skill.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner approves the current branch or PR, or asks to merge or land it into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back once a larger element has lived in production. Use when designing such an element, or when its merge completes it.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose for always-testable rules never converted to checks, and convert the strongest. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, or over prose a growth run just wrote.
- releasing-a-cloudflare-site: How a Cloudflare-served site is released, forced and rolled back. Use when changing the release task, the wrangler config or the analytics loader, and when a release parks.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- requirements-harness: How EdFringeNow runs product/requirements.md as tests under a real headless Chromium - writing leaves and goldens, the harness's determinism traps, the frozen fixtures and golden approval. Use before editing product/requirements.md or anything under product/requirements/.
- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a merged change can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own. Use right after the merge.
- working-with-generated-files: Working with a generated file: naming it, changing the generator rather than the file, resolving conflicts by regenerating. Loaded for any edit of a GENERATED file.
- write-a-requirement-leaf: How a requirement leaf is written in the executable spec, and which kind its case takes. Use when adding or reshaping a requirement line in requirements.md.
- write-a-saga: How a saga case is written: a multi-step story captured as a golden storyboard or animated APNG. Use when authoring or changing a saga case.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a person will execute. Use when filing or editing an issue that asks a human to click, set, register or copy something.
- writing-migration-plans: How a plan's phases are ordered so nothing stalls mid-run. Use before writing any DESIGN.md, migration, rollout or phased plan, or when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written: brevity, structure, triggerability, the provenance marker, a pack's pitch. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md, SKILL.md or manifest, and when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-repo-scanning-checks: How a repo-scanning check picks its files, strips comments, and proves itself silent on real sources. Loaded for any edit of a coded or declared check.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.json or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- writing-wiki-pages: How a product-wiki page is written and grown: key insights, citation, what a source supports, correction without deletion. Loaded for any edit under product-wiki/.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". 14:- `23.1` A full-width timeline of the coming year, one pill per city's festivals, and the trip's dates banded across it.
28:- `23.2` Choosing a festival on the timeline sets the trip's dates to its run plus a day either side.
41:- `23.4` A festival joins the pool only when it is in the same country (and state) as the festival that leads the trip and its city is within reach of it.
55:- `23.5` A festival left out for being out of reach, or in another country, is named in the festivals chip, with how far it is, never dropped silently.
59:- `23.6` Below the site header, the page takes the theme of the festival that leads the trip: its name, and the palette of its genre: comedy, film, theatre or the fringe.
71:- `23.7` The Edinburgh Fringe is a festival like the others: chosen on the timeline, it plans its own programme in its own theme.
85:- `23.8` The trip's first and last day are set on the timeline: drag either end of the band, and the calendar follows.
98:- `23.9` A trip that runs past a festival's own run plans every festival its dates reach, led by the festival chosen while the trip reaches it, else by the one it covers most.
114:- `23.10` When another festival comes to lead the trip, the page's colours fade into its theme rather than jump, unless you ask your device for reduced motion.
128:- `23.11` On a wide screen the page spans the whole window: the timeline and the calendar stretch edge to edge rather than stopping at a content width.
140:- `23.12` Each end of the trip is a line across the strip with a grip at its middle; under the rows the trip is measured like a drawing, its first and last day of the month at the ends of a line the band's width and its length in days between them, clear o

148:- `23.14` The figure moves a little while it stands, cheers whenever you make a choice on the page, and holds still if you ask your device for reduced motion.
160:- `23.15` Pointing at a festival on the strip shows its card: its full name, city and genre, its dates and length, and whether its programme is out yet.
170:- `23.16` The calendar never scrolls sideways: every day of the trip fits the visible width, and no day's column grows wider than 260 pixels.
184:- `23.17` Behind the top of the page is a faded photograph of the city hosting the festival that leads the trip.
198:- `23.18` When another festival comes to lead the trip, its city's photograph fades in over the last one rather than jumping, unless you ask your device for reduced motion.
209:- `23.19` The footer credits the photograph on show: its title, linked to its source, its photographer and its licence, linked to the licence.
213:- `23.20` A country's festivals whose runs meet share one pill (a state's, in a country as large as the United States or Australia): it spans all their runs with each run drawn inside it, carries the country's flag at its middle, and is labelled with how m
231:- `23.21` Pointing at a country's pill shows its card: where, how many festivals, and each one's name and dates.
235:- `23.22` Choosing a country's pill sets the trip to its leading festival's run plus a day either side, and that festival leads the trip.
239:- `23.23` Dragging the band moves the whole trip, keeping its length and the festival chosen; a press that doesn't move still chooses the festival under it.
250:- `23.24` Beside the year, a globe with a place menu under it and nine pictured festival types narrow the festivals it draws, drawn as one piece with the year: the same ring round the globe and the chosen type, and the same capsules for the globe's places,
271:- `23.25` The filters keep a festival only when it matches place, type and subtype, and the festival leading the trip is always kept.
275:- `23.26` Every festival the site lists has a photograph of its city, stored with the site and carrying the title, photographer, licence and source its credit needs.
286:- `23.27` With the place menu on a country, the strip bunches that country's festivals by city instead, so each city's festival can be chosen on its own.
290:- `23.28` However many festivals the year draws, the strip keeps its height: the rows past it scroll inside, faded at the edge to say more are there.
301:- `23.29` Dragging the globe spins it, and let go while still moving it keeps spinning, slowing to a stop.
311:- `23.30` The globe offers areas first, each a badge with its count of festivals; choosing one narrows the year to it and turns and zooms the globe onto it, offering its countries, and a country its cities, while a capsule over the globe steps back out.
325:- `23.31` Choosing a type's picture narrows the year to that type: the picture grows into a header, the other eight shrink into a row under it and the type's subtypes are offered as capsules under them; choosing the header again shows every type.
336:- `23.32` When the page knows which country the reader lives in, a little house stands on it on the globe.
346:- `23.33` Choosing a type moves the pictures rather than swapping them: each glides from where it was to where it goes, the subtypes unfold one after another, and with reduced motion asked for they simply land.
350:- `23.34` Opened with no festival chosen, the page downloads the year's overview and no programme, and asks the reader to choose a festival.
363:- `23.35` Choosing a festival downloads the programmes of that festival and of the festivals in its country (and state) whose runs the trip overlaps, and no other.
375:- `23.36` A festival's card on the strip says how many events its programme holds, once the overview counts them.
379:## 24. How you are getting here
389:- `24.1` Until you have said how you are getting here, a large travel picture sits beside each end of the trip, and clicking either asks beneath the strip where you live, starting from the country you connect from, or that you live in the festival's city.
393:- `24.6` While unsettled, the travel pictures take turns as a plane, a train, a car and a house; asked for reduced motion, they hold still.
397:- `24.7` Each answer settles both travel pictures, and they stop changing: a house living there, a car driving in, a train by rail, and a plane flying in.
401:- `24.9` Living elsewhere, the next question is how you travel: fly, take the train or drive.
405:- `24.10` A travel picture with no room between its end of the trip and the strip's edge is left out, and the one at the other end still asks.
407:- `24.11` The travel pictures and the trip's grips sit at the middle of the strip's visible height, over the festivals beside the trip, and stay there while the festivals scroll.
413:- `24.8` An answer saved before the page asked how you travel is read as one: a home in the festival's city as living there, abroad as flying, anything else as not yet said.
417:- `24.2` The answer decides the trip links: the festival's own city needs no bed, the rest of the country a bed and a train, abroad the airport too.
429:- `24.5` The question is asked once per browser: the answer is stored, and the next festival chosen does not ask again.
433:- `24.4` What a reader saved under `/planJerusalem/` is carried over to the festival planner, once.
437:## 27. Getting there and back
453:- `27.1` Flying in, the travel card shows a flight each way: out on the trip's first day, home on its last, each with the cheapest flight's time, length, stops and price.

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/EdFringeNow/.claude/skills/requirements-harness

# The requirements harness

The framework conventions are the `executable-requirements` pack and the judgment layer is
`spec-driven-product` plus the `writing-tests` skill; layout, lanes and commands are
`product/requirements/README.md`. This carries what those don't: a Playwright golden harness,
and the local approval and fixture policy.

## Writing the spec

- **Laying out `product/requirements.md`** — under each visual leaf its golden is visible and
  uncollapsed; every textual expansion (acceptance notes, proof pointers) is collapsed in a
  `<details>` block. The document is read by sight.

- **Writing a visual leaf's statement** — one line saying what is asserted; the golden carries
  the copy, counts, colours and placement. Anything not visible (a threshold, the rule behind
  the state) goes in a collapsed **Notes** block. (visual-leafs-statement)

- **Choosing a golden's capture** — the smallest surface that proves the leaf: an element crop,
  a clipped region, or a stitched composite, never the whole page or control. The recipe lives on
  the case (`capture: "<selector>"` or `capture(page, tools)`, see `shared/capture-tools.js`);
  whole-page capture is a deliberate exception. (golden-smallest-surface)

- **Proving what an action changes** — capture the same region before and after (and after a
  reload where persistence is the point) and play them as one animated golden (`tools.animate`);
  keep `stitchV`/`stitchH` for things genuinely side by side. (change-time-animation)

- **Encoding an animated golden** — APNG, never GIF (`shared/png.js`'s `encodeAnimated`); the
  comparator compares an animated golden's bytes only. (animated-golden-apng)

- **Placing a leaf both pages follow** — the spec is organised by what the product does, never by
  code layout: a cross-page rule is one feature whose picture shows both the Now page and the
  planner, in the cross-page part after the two page-by-page segments. A case may navigate
  between pages, or open a second page when something fixed at context creation must differ.

- **About to route a leaf to `behavior` or `logic`** — first ask whether it decomposes into
  observable states; a statement joined by "and" usually does, and each part becomes its own
  numbered sub-leaf with its own picture, the parent a heading. When a leaf lands in a coded kind
  because the product makes it invisible, say so in its Notes and name the product change that
  would make it visual.

- **Using `behavior`** — for a gesture's outgoing consequence (a URL built, bytes downloaded,
  storage written) or what the OS paints rather than the page (a native `title` tooltip, a
  cursor). (behavior-rule)

- **Using `logic`** — for a pure rule with no rendered surface; when it is about how values are
  written, declare `table: { columns, rows }` so the gallery renders the table and `verify()`
  proves every row. (logic-rule)

## The browser is part of the expected

- **Bumping the pinned Playwright** — it re-renders every golden, so it is a re-baselining,
  approved like one: the harness refuses any other version (`shared/harness/browser.js`).

- **A comparison that flaps** — add determinism, never a tolerance; the comparator stays at zero
  diff, and the levers (fixed clock, geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network,
  frozen animations, render flags) all live in the harness.

## Traps the harness already paid for

- **Serving the fake origin** — keep it `https://`: geolocation exists only on secure origins,
  and on plain http the app keeps its simulated clock and renders the wrong day.
  (geolocation-exists-only)

- **Moving or denying the fixed geolocation** — the app adopts the device clock only on an
  in-UK fix, so anywhere else renders its pre-set simulated moment, a different day file.
  (app-adopts-device)

- **Captures racing the planner's board animation** — a CSS freeze doesn't stop
  `element.animate`; the harness stubs it to land on end states. (css-freeze-does)

- **Text shifting by a pixel everywhere** — the vendored `fonts.css` resolves against
  `fonts.googleapis.com`, so the vendor route matches on path, host-agnostic. (fonts-arrive-google)

- **Adding an emoji, symbol or script to the product or fixtures** — rebuild the
  `harness/vendor/systemfonts/` subset (its README): Chromium runs under a `FONTCONFIG_FILE`
  that sees only that directory, and a missing glyph renders as tofu. (vendoring-web-fonts)

- **Reproducing a golden flake locally** — compare with the harness's `compare.js`, never a byte
  hash: PNG bytes differ across identical renders, and CI enforces pixels.
  (reproducing-golden-flake)

- **A red `ui-requirements` lane** — its artifact downloads from a host the proxy denies, so read
  which case failed from `get_job_logs` (large `tail_lines`) and re-run it locally;
  `npm run test:ui` writes `.actual.png` / `.diff.png` into `shared/.artifacts/`. (red-ci-lanes)

- **Capturing a floating popup** — set `viewportOnly: true`: a full-page capture scrolls, and
  scrolling dismisses tips, legends and pops. (floating-popup-dies)

- **Waiting for a page to be ready** — wait on the observable state the pages settle into (the
  footer version popup's text, the search placeholder's show count; `case-helpers.js`) plus
  `document.fonts.ready`, never `networkidle`. (ready-networkidle)

- **Capturing hover-driven UI** — open it inside `capture()`, not `drive()`: the runner settles
  the scroll between them, and the scroll fires `mouseleave`. (hover-driven-ui)

- **Capturing right after a click or drag that reflows the layout** — park the pointer
  off-element (`page.mouse.move(0, 0)`) before capturing; left resting, it can land on the next
  element and open its own hover-tip over the shot, non-deterministically between machines.
  (leftover-pointer-hover-tip)

- **Asserting a CSS-transition-driven value** — sample every frame across a bounded window from
  the trigger to the transition's end (a `MutationObserver`/`requestAnimationFrame` loop), never
  one delayed sample gated on the state change; a loaded machine can still miss a single sample.
  (sample-transition-every-frame)

## The fixture freeze

- **Needing data for a case** — use `shared/fixtures/data/`, a frozen snapshot of the real
  committed data cast by the committed builder for state variety; never reach for `site/data/`.
  Every deviation from the source bytes is an `ADJUST` in the builder.

- **Re-running the builder** — it re-casts every golden, so run it only with the owner's
  approval and land builder, fixtures, goldens and gallery in one reviewed change.

- **Having invoked `build-fixtures.js` at all**, even against a scratch edit — it writes into
  `fixtures/data/` as it goes, so `git diff --stat` the whole fixtures dir before deciding there
  is nothing to revert. (build-fixtures-partial-drift)

## Golden approval

- **A golden that no longer matches** — show the owner the committed golden beside
  `shared/.artifacts/<case>.actual.png` and `.diff.png` through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, one
  per item, and say so in the PR body.

- **Landing an intended UI change** — spec edit (doc-first, red), then the implementation, then
  `npm run refresh:ui`, with the refreshed PNGs in the same diff.

# Executable requirements — how this folder works

[`../requirements.md`](../requirements.md) is the numbered UI/UX spec; this
folder makes it executable. Every leaf id in the spec is claimed by exactly one
case here, and the committed expecteds (golden PNGs, coded assertions) are the
owner's approval record of the product. The framework follows the
`executable-requirements` pack standard; the judgment layer (doc-first,
owner-owned expecteds, re-baselining approval) is the `spec-driven-product`
playbook plus the `writing-tests` skill.

## Layout

```
product/
  requirements.md              the numbered spec (config.spec of the pack)
  requirements/
    coverage.test.js           the leaf ⇄ case bijection gate   (default lane)
    gallery.test.js            spec ↔ gallery-lines drift gate  (default lane)
    logic/                     kind: pure product rules          (default lane)
      logic.test.js  cases/<slug>.<id>.case.js
    screen/                    kind: pixel-exact page states     (test:ui lane)
      screen.test.js cases/<slug>.<id>.case.js + <slug>.<id>.png (the goldens)
    behavior/                  kind: driven gestures, coded      (test:ui lane)
      behavior.test.js cases/<slug>.<id>.case.js
    scale/                     kind: bounds on the REAL data     (test:ui lane)
      scale.test.js  cases/<slug>.<id>.case.js
    shared/
      requirements-doc.js kinds.js cases.js     spec parsing + registries
      reference-now.js                          THE pinned instant + fakes
      png.js compare.js artifacts-dir.js        the pixel comparator
      render-case.js refresh.js gallery.js      render/refresh/gallery lanes
      case-helpers.js                           storage seeds, waits, drives
      harness/browser.js                        the hermetic Playwright page
      harness/vendor/                           Leaflet + web fonts, committed
      harness/vendor/systemfonts/               the font jail (see its README)
      fixtures/                                 the frozen dataset + builder
```

- **The folder is the kind.** A case's kind is the directory it lives in; a
  kind is added by dropping `<kind>/kind.js` + a runner — the loader, coverage
  gate and gallery all iterate the registry.
- **Goldens live beside their case**; failure artifacts (actual/diff) go to the
  gitignored `shared/.artifacts/`, never beside the goldens.
- **A golden is the smallest surface that proves its leaf.** A screen case
  declares its scope: `capture: "<selector>"` (a clip at that element's box),
  or `async capture(page, tools)` composing clips and stitches
  (`shared/capture-tools.js` — `element`, `clip`, `unionClip`, `stitchV/H`)
  for composites like one grid lane over three days with its label and pill.
  Omitting `capture` means full-page — a deliberate exception, not a default.
  The spec doc embeds these crops uncollapsed; the words stay folded.

## Lanes

| lane | command | runs | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | `npm test` / `bash scripts/verify.sh` | coverage gate, gallery gate, logic cases | everywhere (no browser) |
| UI | `npm run test:ui` | screen (pixel-exact) + behavior cases, and scale cases against `site/data/` | pinned Playwright Chromium; CI's `ui-requirements` job |
| refresh | `npm run refresh:ui [filter]` | regenerates goldens + the gallery together | after an INTENDED UI change only |

The UI lane runs its cases **concurrently** — `shared/case-concurrency.js`
sizes the pool from the machine, and `REQUIREMENTS_CONCURRENCY` overrides it.
A case's render does not depend on wall-clock timing, so the pool cannot move a
pixel; each case still gets its own browser context. The `--test-concurrency=1`
on the command is what keeps the two lane files from running at once, so the
pool is the whole suite's page budget rather than one per file.

A case waits for **states, not durations**: `settle()` returns once the fonts
are in, every image has decoded and the DOM has held still across consecutive
frames, and `awaitReaction()` covers a consequence that arrives after its
gesture, where the page is briefly quiet in between. A `waitForTimeout` in a
case is a bug — it is either slower than the state it stands for or, on a slow
machine, shorter.

The harness pins Playwright **1.56.1** (`shared/harness/browser.js`) — the
version whose Chromium rendered the committed goldens. The Claude sandbox
ships it globally; CI installs it per run; any other version refuses to
compare. Everything nondeterministic is faked once, in the harness: the clock
(Sat 15 Aug 2026 19:30 Edinburgh), geolocation (central Edinburgh),
`Math.random`, fonts/Leaflet/tiles/geocoder/data (committed vendor + fixture
bytes), CSS + WAAPI animations (frozen), and smooth scrolling (landed

# intro

a=s.index("- `23.1` "); b=s.index("- `23.2` ")
old=s[a:b]
img=re.search(r"  !\[planng-timeline.*\n",old).group(0)
s=s[:a]+("- `23.1` A full-width timeline of the coming year, each festival a bar on rows of its own with its name beside it, and the trip's dates banded across it.\n\n"+img+
"""
  <details><summary>Notes</summary>

  Twelve months from the start of the month before today. Bars are never
  drawn over one another, and a festival's name runs beside its bar only while
  the year draws ten festivals or fewer and every name fits the rows (23.38
  covers a crowded year). An edition whose programme is not published yet is
  drawn hollow, and is still chosen like any other. The bar of the festival
  that leads the trip is lit. Nothing sits beneath the year: the trip's days
  are written on the band (23.12) and the way there and back sits beside it
  (section 24).
  </details>

""")+s[b:]
# retire pills, drill, scrolling rows
for leaf,nxt in [("- `23.20` ","- `23.23` "),("- `23.27` ","- `23.29` ")]:
    cut(leaf,nxt)
# 23.24
a=s.index("- `23.24` "); b=s.index("- `23.25` ")
old=s[a:b]
img=re.search(r"  !\[planng-strip-filter.*\n",old).group(0)
s=s[:a]+("- `23.24` The year sits between nine pictured festival types on its left and a desk globe on its right, both as tall as its rows and level with the first of them, and together they narrow the festivals it draws.\n\n"+img+
"""
  <details><summary>Notes</summary>

  A place is an area (the British Isles, Europe, the Middle East and so
  on, `site/planNG/lib/areas.js`), a country or one of its cities, each chosen
  on the globe; a type is one of nine: film, music, theatre, dance, comedy,
  art & books (the registry's `art` and `literature`), mixed arts (`fringe`
  and `multi`), sports and academic; a subtype is what sets one festival apart
  within its type (`film-documentary`, `academic-biology`), a label on the
  festival and never on its events. The globe is a desk globe: tan land on a
  deep blue sea, shaded as a sphere, held in a brass ring on a wooden stand,
  the countries with a festival in the page's colour. Each type's picture
  carries how many festivals the chosen place holds of it, and a type with
  none is drawn faded; its name is on its card (23.41). On a narrow screen the
  types and the globe sit side by side above the year. Only the strip is
  narrowed: the pool the calendar drafts from is the trip's, whatever the
  filters say.
  </details>

""")+s[b:]
# new leaves after 23.36
a=s.index("- `23.36` "); b=s.index("## 24.",a)
new="""- `23.37` The year's rows take the most searched festivals first: each goes on a row where it keeps clear of its neighbours, a festival of a week or more on the free row holding the fewest such, until the rows are 70% full.

  🔧 _Logic leaf._ <!-- req-gallery:23.37 -->

  <details><summary>Notes</summary>

  How searched a festival is comes from the registry: its `popularity` where
  the festival finder has measured it, else the events its programme holds,
  and a longer run first among equals. The festival leading the trip always
  takes the first place. A festival that fits no row is passed over for the
  next. Ranking and filling are redone inside whatever the filters leave.
  </details>

- `23.38` In a crowded year the rows carry bars without names, and every festival they leave out is drawn faintly behind them in its type's colour.

  ![planng-year-crowd.23.38](requirements/screen/cases/planng-year-crowd.23.38.png) <!-- req-gallery:23.38 -->

  <details><summary>Notes</summary>

  The strip has as many rows as fit the height of the types and the globe,
  and never scrolls; a faint festival is placed anywhere across that height,
  at its own dates. No text sits under the rows.
  </details>

- `23.39` Changing a filter moves the festivals rather than redrawing them: a festival still drawn glides to its new place, one promoted from behind grows into its row, and the rest fade out or in.

  🚩 _Behavior leaf._ <!-- req-gallery:23.39 -->

  <details><summary>Notes</summary>

  With reduced motion asked for they simply land.
  </details>

- `23.40` Pointing along the year magnifies the weeks under the pointer, as a dock does, and a bar grown wide enough there shows its name.

  ![planng-year-lens.23.40](requirements/screen/cases/planng-year-lens.23.40.png) <!-- req-gallery:23.40 -->

- `23.41` Pointing at a type's picture shows its card: its name, how many festivals it holds, its subtypes and the next of its festivals.

  ![planng-type-card.23.41](requirements/screen/cases/planng-type-card.23.41.png) <!-- req-gallery:23.41 -->

"""
s=s[:b]+new+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

# Committing

- **One concern per commit.** If two changes could each stand alone, split them; a message that
  wants numbered items is the split talking.
- **Reference the issue, when the change has one** — `Refs #n`, or `Fixes #n` / `Closes #n` where
  the commit finishes it. A change tracked by its PR alone references nothing.
- **A landed commit is revised by a new commit**, never a rewrite of that one.
- **Stage by name** — `git add <paths>` for the files this commit is about; `-a` sweeps in whatever
  else was in progress.

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: - **Original ask (done):** make downloads lighter. The page loads only the festival overview first, and after a pick it downloads only programmes from the same country. This shipped as PR #985: merged via squash as 3f85c7c, then released by the "Website release" thread. - **Design discussion, mockups only:** a redesign of the planner's year strip. The agreed design is saved in memory at `[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_COWORK_MEMORY_PATH_OVERRIDE]/team/silo/planng-year-strip-design.md`. It covers these points: - **No grouping:** no grouping by geography or type; those are filters. - **Ranking:** festivals are ranked by popularity, with Google result count as the proxy. - **Rows:** thin rows (bars about 12px). The most popular festival goes first, each on the first row where it fits with a gap. A long festival (7 days or more) goes on the free row holding the fewest long festivals. Filling stops when the rows are 70% full. Ariel chose 70% twice, including again with more rows. - **Background:** everything else is drawn faint behind the rows, across the whole height, in a desaturated, transparent version of its type colour. - **Text:** no text on the grid when it is crowded; names appear on hover. Text shows only when the filter leaves about 10 or fewer festivals. - **Per filter:** ranking and filling are recomputed inside the current filter. - **Animation:** changing a filter animates. Festivals are added or removed, and promoted from or demoted to the background. - **Magnifier:** hovering gives a dock-style fisheye; a bar that grows wide enough shows its name. - **Height:** the whole bar is one height, set by the controls. Drop the place dropdown under the globe. Drop the labels under the type tiles and replace them with a hover popup showing name, festival count, subtypes and the next festival. The strip gets as many rows as fit, with no text line under it. - **Placement:** type tiles on the left, globe on the right. Both are top-aligned with the first row of festivals, not with the month axis. - **Globe look:** a physical desk globe. Tan land on deep-blue sea, sphere shading with a highlight, a tilted brass meridian ring and a small wooden stand. - Earlier, Ariel said "No need to implement that". - **Latest ask (Ariel, 2026-10-02 17:30):** "I thought you implemented all the new design already. Please do that." I am now implementing the full design in the real planner. 2. Key Technical Concepts: - **Spec-driven development:** `product/requirements.md` holds leaves. Each leaf is proved by exactly one case: logic, screen (golden PNG) or behavior. A coverage gate and a gallery gate enforce this, and doc-first means the spec goes red before the code. - **Leaf ids** are never reused. Retired leaves and their cases are removed. - **Commands:** - `npm test` runs the default lane. - `npm run test:ui` runs the Playwright screen and behavior cases. - `npm run refresh:ui` regenerates goldens and the gallery after an intended UI change. Goldens that move need owner approval; show them in the PR. - **Fixtures:** the fixture registry has only 4 festivals (acco, edfringe, haifa-iff, jerusalem-comedy), and fixtures are frozen. A crowded year needs a routed registry; `routeCrowdedYear` exists in `case-helpers.js`. - **Harness:** freezes CSS and WAAPI animations; uses the pinned Playwright 1.56.1. - **i18n:** `site/planNG/i18n/translations.js` (en, he, ru, ja). Localized pages are generated with `node scripts/localize-pages.mjs`. - **Types:** from `TYPES` in `site/planNG/lib/festival-filter.js`, mapped with `typeOfKind(kind)`. - **Type colours:** the first gradient stop of each icon SVG: | Type | Colour | |---|---| | academic | #3b82f6 | | art | #14b8a6 | | comedy | #facc15 | | dance | #ec4899 | | film | #ef4444 | | mixed | #6366f1 | | music | #9b5cf6 | | sports | #22c55e | | theatre | #f59e0b | - **Serving locally:** serve `site/` with `python3 -m http.server 8000`. Import Playwright from `/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs` and route `unpkg.com` to abort. The mock server runs on port 8123 in `scratchpad/mock`. - **Thread attachments:** the thread hit the limit of 24 attached outputs, so further files must be linked as `[name](/mnt/project-files/...)`. 3. Files and Code Sections: - **`product/requirements.md`** (committed 5fc6acd, "Spec the year strip redesign…"): - Intro reworded: "drawn at its dates, the most searched on rows of their own and the rest faint behind them". - 23.1 rewritten: "A full-width timeline of the coming year, each festival a bar on rows of its own with its name beside it, and the trip's dates banded across it." Its notes say names show while ≤10 festivals and every name fits. - Removed leaves 23.20, 23.21, 23.22, 23.27 and 23.28. - 23.24 rewritten: types on the left, a desk globe on the right, both as tall as the rows and level with the first row. The notes describe the desk globe and say the type name lives on its card (23.41). - New leaves: - 23.37: a logic leaf for the row rules. Popularity is `popularity`, else `events`, else unknown; a longer run wins among equals; the leading festival goes first. - 23.38: a screen leaf, `planng-year-crowd.23.38.png`, for the crowded year (rows plus faint background, no scroll, no text under the strip). - 23.39: a behavior leaf for filter changes that glide, grow or fade. Reduced motion lands without animating. - 23.40: a screen leaf, `planng-year-lens.23.40.png`, for the magnifier. - 23.41: a screen leaf, `planng-type-card.23.41.png`, for the type card. - **Removed cases** (`git rm`, committed in 5fc6acd): - `screen/cases/planng-city-pill.23.20.*` - `screen/cases/planng-city-card.23.21.*` - `behavior/cases/planng-city-pick.23.22.case.js` - `screen/cases/planng-country-drill.23.27.*` - `screen/cases/planng-year-height.23.28.*` - **`product/requirements/logic/cases/planng-strip-rows.23.37.case.js`** (new; this was the latest committed state): - TABLE rows: `["Fringe 0–40 (900), Acco 10–20 (50), Haifa 50–55 (300)","2","none","1: Fringe, Haifa · 2: Acco"]`, `["Fringe 0–30 (900), Haifa 40–70 (300), Acco 80–84 (50)","2","none","1: Fringe, Acco · 2: Haifa"]`, `["Fringe 0–30 (900), Haifa 35–72 (300), Acco 75–80 (50)","1","none","1: Fringe, Haifa"]`, `["Fringe 0–50 (900), Acco 20–30 (300), Haifa 60–65 (50)","1","none","1: Fringe, Haifa"]`, the same with leading "Acco" giving "1: Acco, Haifa", and `["Fringe 0–10 (unknown), Acco 20–40 (unknown), Haifa 50–55 (40)","1","none","1: Haifa, Acco, Fringe"]`. - `verify` imports `rankBars` and `fillRows` from `site/planNG/lib/timeline.js`. It calls `fillRows(ranked.map(bar=>({from:bar.start*100,to:bar.end*100,long:bar.end-bar.start>=0.07})),{rows,width:100,gap:2,fill:0.7})`. - It failed before the implementation and now passes. - **`site/planNG/lib/timeline.js`** (uncommitted). Added before `timelineBunches`: ```js function searchedOf(bar){const measured=bar.festival.popularity ?? bar.edition.events; return measured==null?-1:measured;} export function rankBars(bars, focusKey){ return [...bars].sort((a,b)=> Number(b.key===focusKey)-Number(a.key===focusKey) || searchedOf(b)-searchedOf(a) || (b.end-b.start)-(a.end-a.start) || a.start-b.start); } export function fillRows(extents,{rows,width,gap,fill}){ const taken=Array.from({length:rows},()=>[]); const longs=new Array(rows).fill(0); let used=0; return extents.map(({from,to,long})=>{ if(used>=fill*rows*width) return -1; const free=taken.flatMap((claims,row)=>claims.every(([a,b])=>to+gap<=a||from>=b+gap)?[row]:[]); if(!free.length) return -1; const row=long?free.reduce((best,r)=>longs[r]` building in `renderStripFilters` (`opt`, `byName`, `areaGroups`, `$("timelinePlace")`) and updated its comment. - Removed the `timelineFilters` change listener and the flagSvg import. - `cityPlace` is still used by the globe. Translation keys `filter.place`, `filter.anyPlace`, `filter.allOf` and `bunch.*` may now be unused and need checking. - **`site/planNG/flags.js`:** deleted with `git rm`; nothing else used it. - **`site/planNG/index.html`:** still has `
` at line 80 and a comment mentioning "a place menu". Both need removing, the desk globe stand SVG adding in `.tl-place`, and the localized he, ru and ja pages regenerating. - **`site/planNG/planNG.css`:** not yet edited. Relevant spots: - `.timeline` grid (line about 1592), `areas "place main types"`. - `.tl-place` and `.tl-types` both have `margin-top:-22px`. - `.tl-lens` globe variables (light-dark sea #e4f0fa and so on, `--globe-ring:var(--violet)`). - `.tl-type-name` styles. - The mobile block at max-width 620px (areas "place types" "main main"). - `.tl-filter` select styles. - `.tl-rows` scroll CSS (line about 2040, with max-height and mask fades). - `.tl-item`, `.tl-bar`, `.tl-label`, `.tl-item--bunch`, `.tl-run` and `.tl-flag` (lines about 2156–2235). - **Behavior and screen cases that reference the strip:** - `case-helpers.js` lines 228 and 267 use `.tl-item[data-festival=…]`. - 23.15, 23.2, 23.5 (far-away count), 23.34, 23.23, 23.35 and 23.36 reference strip items. - 24.11 (`planng-way-middle.24.11`) references `.tl-rows` scrolling. Leaf 24.11 says the pictures "stay there while the festivals scroll" and may need rewording. - **Memory file** `[REDACTED:env:CLAUDE_COWORK_MEMORY_PATH_OVERRIDE]/team/silo/planng-year-strip-design.md` holds the full design spec; it was updated several times. - **Mockups** in `/mnt/project-files/strip-groups/`: `overview-*`, `prominence-*`, `popular-*`, `thin-*`, `bar-*`, `tall-*`, `rows-compare.png`, `opt7-*`, `swap-1.png`, `globe-1.png`, `globe-zoom*.png`, `spread-0.png`, `spread-1.png`. - **Prototype artifact:** https://claude.ai/artifact/TMjQmooGEKkvipxvfWAL96 (scratchpad `mock/strip-prototype.html`). The mock driver scripts live in the scratchpad (`globe.mjs`, `bar4.mjs`, `mock/strip2.html`). The desk-globe CSS and SVG from the mock: - Lens scale 0.8; sea #3d7fb8, deep #16466f, land #e3cf96; shading via a radial-gradient `::after`. - Brass gradient #f6dc8c → #c9952e → #7a5414. The meridian arc is drawn with `rotate(23 82 66)`. - Brass stem; wooden base ellipse with gradient #9a6337 → #4f2c12. 4. Errors and fixes: - **Thread attachment limit:** the thread reached 24 attached outputs, so later images are linked by path in the reply text. - **Push rejected:** `--force-with-lease` was rejected with "stale info" because the remote branch had been deleted after the #985 merge. Fixed with `git remote prune origin` and a plain `git push -u`. - **Mock fixes:** - Duplicate `ROWS` declaration in the mock: renamed to NROW. - Globe colours did not apply when injected after load (the canvas reads its variables at init): fixed by injecting the CSS via `addInitScript`. - Several quoting bugs in the sed edits to the mock driver were fixed. - **Hook blocks:** - Using curl in Bash requires the `fetching-from-the-web` skill. It was loaded after a Stop-hook blocking finding, and curl is now avoided. - The Stop hook also noted an advisory: don't request review from missingbulb, the PR author. - **Option C rework:** a first C variant at 30% came out identical to B (55 coloured), so I changed C to 45% (88 coloured) before showing Ariel. 5. Problem Solving: - The design was settled through rounds of mockups with Ariel. - Popularity has no real data source yet. The chosen default is `festival.popularity ?? edition.events`, with unknown ranked below known and a longer run first among equals. The PR description should say so. - The lens distorts the bars and months, but not the trip band or handles. This also needs a mention in the PR. - Faint festivals are non-interactive (tabIndex -1, aria-hidden). 6. All user messages (since the earlier summary): - "So here's the thing - none of those work. None of those can give a good overview of festivals pre-filtering, because the bunching strategy creates too many groups, and the text display uses too much of the space. Both need to be handled. First - we need to understand what does a person, pre-filtering, wants to understand from the annual festival view. Perhaps showing only "major festivals" and other festivals in a faded background does the trick. And certainly we can't afford to put any text on the grid there. Only if the filters did a great job and you can fit the 10 remainig festivals on 4-5 rows with text. But if it's crowded - no way." - "Also, if we do a good job at finding all the "festivals" in the world - there'll be many there almost regardless of filter." - "No, you're taking geography filters and using them as grouping. That's a bad direction, because once we filter by geography - that strategy doesn't help you. The grouping should be somethign else, not expressed by the festival class or geography." - "What if there was a way to highlight "important" festivals? Let's assume there is (number of google search results is a good proxy), and then we use that to draw festivals, on, let's say, 3 rows of events, starting with the most popular, and taking a reasonable space between them, try to place the second most popular, and go down the list until the lines are 70% full. Some of the other festivals can be drawn in the background, grayed out. Possibly not adhereing to the 3 lines (so use the space behind them liberally." - Decision card tap: chose "70%". - "Also make the 3 lines thinner. And if you can draw the background in (much milder then, transparent, greyish) foreground colors." - "Also make sure that when we change the filter - the items are added and removed (or promoted from background) with animations." - "Also can you show me the full bar with the globe and class filters?" - "Also - I think I want a magnifying glass effect on the "festivals galary", so where the mouse cursor is - the display is zoomed (much like the macos actions bar)." - "Ok, so we're learning that the hieght of the full bar should be a visual requirement for all 3 controls. So perhaps we add more lines to the gallary until it fits? And maybe drop the text below the classes (on hover - popup with information on the class, number of festivals, subclasses, etc), and drop the dropdown from below the globe?" - "Certainly the text below the gallary should be dropped." - "For you question - show me samples to choose visually." - "1. 70%. 2. Switch the globe and the classes buttons. 3. Please align the globe and classes controls with the first line of festivals in the gallary, not the top part, which is very quiet visually." - "Can you make the globe look like a physical globe? I think it adds fanfare." - "Also, when placing the festivals - it sesms like the top row has all the long ones. We you place a long festival, and you can put it on different rwos - please select the one with the least long festivals." - "lgtm and release the website" (applied to #985: merged, and the release handled by the Website release thread) - "I thought you implemented all the new design already. Please do that." 7. Pending Tasks: - Implement the full strip redesign on branch `claude/split-data-by-country-pl4zgq`, PR #1002 (https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/1002), which is subscribed to PR events. Steps: - CSS for strip items: type colours, faint style, transitions, named and crowded modes, lens, magnified labels inside bars. Remove the scroll and pill CSS. - Swap the grid areas to "types main place" and set the controls' margin-top to about 26px. - Hide the tile names in the grid, keeping them visually hidden and keeping the header name. - Type hover card for 23.41, with new i18n keys in 4 languages. - Desk globe: lens CSS variables, the brass ring colour, a shading overlay, and the stand SVG in `index.html`. - Remove `#timelinePlace` and regenerate the localized pages. - Remove `timelineBunches`, `bunchPlace` and `stackRows` and their tests, and any unused i18n keys. - Set the rows to fit the controls' height, probably 9×20=180px. - Write the cases: - 23.38: screen, with a routed crowded registry (possibly a new `routeWorldYear` helper). - 23.39: behavior. Filter change keeps the same element node; promoted or faint items transition. - 23.40: screen, with the lens hover in `capture()`. - 23.41: screen, type card. - Fix the affected existing cases and leaves (24.11 scroll wording, 23.5, and others). - Run `npm test` and `npm run test:ui`, then `npm run refresh:ui` for the intended golden changes. Look at the page in the browser. - Commit, push and update the PR body. The body needs Before/After, the popularity fallback, the lens scope, and the goldens that moved. Then reply in the thread with a one-line folders-touched box and a link. - Keep the status checklist updated with `update_status`. 8. Current Work: I was midway through implementing the redesign. The spec commit is pushed and PR #1002 is open. The logic for 23.37 is implemented in `lib/timeline.js` and green. `timeline-view.js` has been rewritten and the bunch and place-menu removals in `planNG.js` are done. `flags.js` is deleted. None of this is committed yet. My last action was reading the type icon colours to define CSS type colours for the strip bars, just before editing `planNG.css`. The status checklist currently shows "✱ Building popularity rows with faint background". 9. Optional Next Step: Continue implementing per Ariel's "I thought you implemented all the new design already. Please do that." Next, edit `site/planNG/planNG.css`: - Add `--type-*` colours from the icon stops. - Style `.tl-item` and `.tl-bar` with the per-type colour from `[data-type]`, plus `.is-faint` at about 0.22 opacity with saturate 0.45. - Add transitions on inset-inline-start, top, width, height and opacity, disabled under `.tl-track.is-lens` and under reduced motion. - Add `.is-entering` and `.is-leaving` at opacity 0. - Label: absolutely positioned after the bar, before it for late items, and visibility hidden unless `.tl-track.is-named` or `.is-magnified` (inside the bar, in white). - Remove the `.tl-rows` scroll, bunch, run and flag CSS. - Swap grid areas, set margin-top 26px, add the desk globe variables and stand, hide tile names, and remove `.tl-filter`. - Then update `index.html` (remove `#timelinePlace`, add the stand SVG), add the type card, write cases 23.38–23.41, and run the tests. If you need specific details from before compaction (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /root/.claude/projects/-home-user-EdFringeNow/7d0cc264-5989-5725-9feb-3023bc2af913.jsonl Continue the conversation from where it left off without asking the user any further questions. Resume directly — do not acknowledge the summary, do not recap what was happening, do not preface with "I'll continue" or similar. Pick up the last task as if the break never happened.

6	 * pixels; nothing here touches the DOM, so the rules are testable as rules.
7	 *
8	 * One bar per edition, always: an edition is drawn from the registry's dates,
9	 * never from its programme, so a festival of ten thousand performances costs
10	 * the timeline exactly what a festival of ten does.
11	 */
12	
13	const DAY_MS = 86400000;
14	const ms = (iso) => Date.parse(`${iso}T00:00:00Z`);
15	const iso = (t) => new Date(t).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
16	
17	/**
18	 * Twelve whole months, starting with the month before today's — so a festival
19	 * that has just finished is still on screen, and next year's is too.
20	 * @returns {{from: string, to: string, days: number}} inclusive ISO dates
21	 */
22	export function timelineSpan(todayISO) {
23	  const [y, m] = todayISO.split("-").map(Number);
24	  const start = Date.UTC(y, m - 2, 1);
25	  const end = Date.UTC(y, m + 10, 1) - DAY_MS;
26	  return { from: iso(start), to: iso(end), days: Math.round((end - start) / DAY_MS) + 1 };
27	}
28	
29	/** Where a day's start falls along the span, 0..1. */
30	export function dayFrac(span, dateISO) {
31	  return (ms(dateISO) - ms(span.from)) / (span.days * DAY_MS);
32	}
33	
34	/** The first day of each month in the span, with where it falls. */
35	export function monthTicks(span) {
36	  const ticks = [];
37	  const [y, m] = span.from.split("-").map(Number);
38	  for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) {
39	    const at = iso(Date.UTC(y, m - 1 + i, 1));
40	    ticks.push({ date: at, frac: dayFrac(span, at) });
41	  }
42	  return ticks;
43	}
44	
45	/**
46	 * One bar per edition that overlaps the span.
47	 * @param {{festivals: object[]}} registry site/data/festivals/index.json
48	 * @returns {{key, festival, edition, start, end, hasData}[]} `start`/`end` are
49	 *   fractions of the span, clipped to it; `end` covers the last day whole
50	 */
51	export function timelineBars(registry, span) {
52	  const bars = [];
53	  for (const festival of registry.festivals) {
54	    for (const edition of festival.editions) {
55	      if (edition.lastDate < span.from || edition.firstDate > span.to) continue;
56	      const start = Math.max(0, dayFrac(span, edition.firstDate));
57	      const end = Math.min(1, dayFrac(span, edition.lastDate) + 1 / span.days);
58	      bars.push({
59	        key: editionKey(festival.id, edition.id),
60	        festival,
61	        edition,
62	        start,
63	        end,
64	        hasData: Boolean(edition.dataUrl),
65	      });
66	    }
67	  }
68	  return bars.sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start || a.festival.id.localeCompare(b.festival.id));
69	}
70	
71	/* How searched a festival is: what the festival finder measured, else the
72	 * events its programme holds; unknown ranks below every known count. */
73	function searchedOf(bar) {
74	  const measured = bar.festival.popularity ?? bar.edition.events;
75	  return measured == null ? -1 : measured;
76	}
77	
78	/**
79	 * The bars in the order the year's rows take them: the festival leading the
80	 * trip first, then the most searched, a longer run first among equals.
81	 * @param {object[]} bars from timelineBars()
82	 * @param {string|null} focusKey
83	 * @returns {object[]} a sorted copy
84	 */
85	export function rankBars(bars, focusKey) {
86	  return [...bars].sort(
87	    (a, b) =>
88	      Number(b.key === focusKey) - Number(a.key === focusKey) ||
89	      searchedOf(b) - searchedOf(a) ||
90	      b.end - b.start - (a.end - a.start) ||
91	      a.start - b.start
92	  );
93	}
94	
95	/**
96	 * Which row each festival takes, in the order given, until the rows are
97	 * `fill` full. A festival keeps `gap` clear of its neighbours on its row; a
98	 * long one goes to the free row holding the fewest long ones, any other to
99	 * the first free row; one that fits no row is passed over.
100	 * @param {{from: number, to: number, long?: boolean}[]} extents in rank order
101	 * @param {{rows: number, width: number, gap: number, fill: number}} o
102	 * @returns {number[]} each festival's row, or -1 for one left off the rows
103	 */
104	export function fillRows(extents, { rows, width, gap, fill }) {
105	  const taken = Array.from({ length: rows }, () => []);
106	  const longs = new Array(rows).fill(0);
107	  let used = 0;
108	  return extents.map(({ from, to, long }) => {
109	    if (used >= fill * rows * width) return -1;
110	    const free = taken.flatMap((claims, row) => (claims.every(([a, b]) => to + gap <= a || from >= b + gap) ? [row] : []));
111	    if (!free.length) return -1;
112	    const row = long ? free.reduce((best, r) => (longs[r] < longs[best] ? r : best), free[0]) : free[0];
113	    taken[row].push([from, to]);
114	    if (long) longs[row]++;
115	    used += to - from + gap;
116	    return row;
117	  });
118	}
119	
120	/**
121	 * The bars bunched by country: every edition in one country whose runs meet
122	 * (or come within `joinDays` of each other) is one pill, so a country holding
123	 * seven festivals at once costs the strip one row, not seven. A festival that
124	 * names a `region` (a state of a country as large as the US) bunches with
125	 * that region's alone. `placeOf` swaps in another grouping, such as
126	 * cityPlace() once the strip shows a single country.
127	 *
128	 * A bunch is led by the edition with a published programme and the longest
129	 * run, then the one that starts first: the one a reader most likely came for.
130	 * @returns {{key, lead, bars, start, end, hasData}[]} `key` is the lead's
131	 *   edition key; `bars` are the bunch's, in start order; `start`/`end` span them
132	 */
133	export function timelineBunches(registry, span, placeOf = bunchPlace, joinDays = 7) {
134	  const join = joinDays / span.days;
135	  const open = new Map();
136	  const bunches = [];
137	  for (const bar of timelineBars(registry, span)) {
138	    const place = placeOf(bar.festival);
139	    const last = open.get(place);
140	    if (last && bar.start <= last.end + join) {
141	      last.bars.push(bar);
142	      last.end = Math.max(last.end, bar.end);
143	      continue;
144	    }
145	    const bunch = { bars: [bar], start: bar.start, end: bar.end };
146	    open.set(place, bunch);
147	    bunches.push(bunch);
148	  }
149	  return bunches.map((b) => {
150	    const lead = [...b.bars].sort(
151	      (x, y) => Number(y.hasData) - Number(x.hasData) || y.end - y.start - (x.end - x.start) || x.start - y.start
152	    )[0];
153	    return { key: lead.key, lead, bars: b.bars, start: b.start, end: b.end, hasData: b.bars.some((x) => x.hasData) };
154	  });
155	}
156	
157	/** Where a festival bunches: its region where it names one, else its country. */
158	export function bunchPlace(festival) {
159	  return festival.region ? `${festival.country}|${festival.region}` : festival.country;
160	}
161	
162	/** The one spelling of "this edition of this festival" the page keys on. */
163	export function editionKey(festivalId, editionId) {
164	  return `${festivalId}@${editionId}`;
165	}
166	
167	/**
168	 * Rows for the bars, so no two overlap. Each bar claims the stretch its bar
169	 * and its label cover together; a bar goes on the first row whose last claim
170	 * ended before this one starts.
171	 * @param {{from: number, to: number}[]} extents in any unit, one per bar, in
172	 *   the bars' order
173	 * @param {number} gap the space two claims on one row must keep between them
174	 * @returns {number[]} the row of each bar
175	 */
176	export function stackRows(extents, gap = 0) {
177	  const rowEnds = [];
178	  return extents.map(({ from, to }) => {
179	    let row = rowEnds.findIndex((end) => end + gap <= from);
180	    if (row === -1) {
181	      row = rowEnds.length;
182	      rowEnds.push(to);
183	    } else {
184	      rowEnds[row] = to;
185	    }
186	    return row;
187	  });
188	}
189	
</system-reminder>

---
name: planng-year-strip-design
description: Ariel's agreed design for the planNG year festival strip (popularity rows + faint background), not yet built
metadata:
  type: project
  modified: 2026-10-02T15:07:09.363Z
---

Agreed with Ariel 2026-10-02 in the "lighter downloads" thread; mockups in /mnt/project-files/strip-groups/thin-*.png. Not implemented yet; Ariel said build only when asked.

- No grouping by geography or festival class: those are filters (chips), and grouping by them breaks once you filter by them.
- Rank festivals by popularity (proxy: Google search result count; needs a per-festival number from the festival finder, which needs a search API key).
- Three thin rows (~12px bars). Place most popular first into the first row where it clears neighbours by a gap; skip ones that don't fit; a long festival (7+ days) goes to the fitting row holding the fewest long festivals, so long ones don't stack in the top row; stop when rows are 70% full (Ariel chose 70% over 40%).
- Everything else drawn behind, freely across the whole strip height, as faint, desaturated, transparent versions of their type colour.
- No text on the grid when crowded; names on hover. Text only when the filter leaves ~10 or fewer.
- Ranking and fill are recomputed inside the current filter.
- Changing a filter must animate: items added, removed, or promoted from background into a row (and demoted) with transitions.
- Hovering the strip magnifies the weeks under the cursor (macOS Dock style fisheye); names appear only on enlarged bars. Prototype: https://claude.ai/artifact/TMjQmooGEKkvipxvfWAL96
- Bar height is one visual requirement for all three controls, set by the globe: drop the place dropdown under the globe, drop the labels under the type tiles (hover popup: name, festival count, subtypes, next one), and give the strip as many rows as fit (9 at the tile grid's height), filled to 70% (Ariel chose 70% again with more rows). No text line under the strip. Type tiles on the left, globe on the right; both top-aligned with the first row of festivals, not the month axis.
- The globe looks like a physical desk globe: tan land on deep-blue sea, sphere shading with a highlight, a tilted brass meridian ring and a small wooden stand, all within the bar height (globe shrinks to ~130px).

**Why:** pre-filter, users want where/when it's busy and which landmarks fall there; the old country-chained groups made too many groups and too much text.
**How to apply:** use this as the spec when the strip redesign is requested; write each bullet as a requirement leaf.

# Committing

- **One concern per commit.** If two changes could each stand alone, split them; a message that
  wants numbered items is the split talking.
- **Reference the issue, when the change has one** — `Refs #n`, or `Fixes #n` / `Closes #n` where
  the commit finishes it. A change tracked by its PR alone references nothing.
- **A landed commit is revised by a new commit**, never a rewrite of that one.
- **Stage by name** — `git add <paths>` for the files this commit is about; `-a` sweeps in whatever
  else was in progress.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/EdFringeNow/.claude/skills/requirements-harness

# The requirements harness

The framework conventions are the `executable-requirements` pack and the judgment layer is
`spec-driven-product` plus the `writing-tests` skill; layout, lanes and commands are
`product/requirements/README.md`. This carries what those don't: a Playwright golden harness,
and the local approval and fixture policy.

## Writing the spec

- **Laying out `product/requirements.md`** — under each visual leaf its golden is visible and
  uncollapsed; every textual expansion (acceptance notes, proof pointers) is collapsed in a
  `<details>` block. The document is read by sight.

- **Writing a visual leaf's statement** — one line saying what is asserted; the golden carries
  the copy, counts, colours and placement. Anything not visible (a threshold, the rule behind
  the state) goes in a collapsed **Notes** block. (visual-leafs-statement)

- **Choosing a golden's capture** — the smallest surface that proves the leaf: an element crop,
  a clipped region, or a stitched composite, never the whole page or control. The recipe lives on
  the case (`capture: "<selector>"` or `capture(page, tools)`, see `shared/capture-tools.js`);
  whole-page capture is a deliberate exception. (golden-smallest-surface)

- **Proving what an action changes** — capture the same region before and after (and after a
  reload where persistence is the point) and play them as one animated golden (`tools.animate`);
  keep `stitchV`/`stitchH` for things genuinely side by side. (change-time-animation)

- **Encoding an animated golden** — APNG, never GIF (`shared/png.js`'s `encodeAnimated`); the
  comparator compares an animated golden's bytes only. (animated-golden-apng)

- **Placing a leaf both pages follow** — the spec is organised by what the product does, never by
  code layout: a cross-page rule is one feature whose picture shows both the Now page and the
  planner, in the cross-page part after the two page-by-page segments. A case may navigate
  between pages, or open a second page when something fixed at context creation must differ.

- **About to route a leaf to `behavior` or `logic`** — first ask whether it decomposes into
  observable states; a statement joined by "and" usually does, and each part becomes its own
  numbered sub-leaf with its own picture, the parent a heading. When a leaf lands in a coded kind
  because the product makes it invisible, say so in its Notes and name the product change that
  would make it visual.

- **Using `behavior`** — for a gesture's outgoing consequence (a URL built, bytes downloaded,
  storage written) or what the OS paints rather than the page (a native `title` tooltip, a
  cursor). (behavior-rule)

- **Using `logic`** — for a pure rule with no rendered surface; when it is about how values are
  written, declare `table: { columns, rows }` so the gallery renders the table and `verify()`
  proves every row. (logic-rule)

## The browser is part of the expected

- **Bumping the pinned Playwright** — it re-renders every golden, so it is a re-baselining,
  approved like one: the harness refuses any other version (`shared/harness/browser.js`).

- **A comparison that flaps** — add determinism, never a tolerance; the comparator stays at zero
  diff, and the levers (fixed clock, geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network,
  frozen animations, render flags) all live in the harness.

## Traps the harness already paid for

- **Serving the fake origin** — keep it `https://`: geolocation exists only on secure origins,
  and on plain http the app keeps its simulated clock and renders the wrong day.
  (geolocation-exists-only)

- **Moving or denying the fixed geolocation** — the app adopts the device clock only on an
  in-UK fix, so anywhere else renders its pre-set simulated moment, a different day file.
  (app-adopts-device)

- **Captures racing the planner's board animation** — a CSS freeze doesn't stop
  `element.animate`; the harness stubs it to land on end states. (css-freeze-does)

- **Text shifting by a pixel everywhere** — the vendored `fonts.css` resolves against
  `fonts.googleapis.com`, so the vendor route matches on path, host-agnostic. (fonts-arrive-google)

- **Adding an emoji, symbol or script to the product or fixtures** — rebuild the
  `harness/vendor/systemfonts/` subset (its README): Chromium runs under a `FONTCONFIG_FILE`
  that sees only that directory, and a missing glyph renders as tofu. (vendoring-web-fonts)

- **Reproducing a golden flake locally** — compare with the harness's `compare.js`, never a byte
  hash: PNG bytes differ across identical renders, and CI enforces pixels.
  (reproducing-golden-flake)

- **A red `ui-requirements` lane** — its artifact downloads from a host the proxy denies, so read
  which case failed from `get_job_logs` (large `tail_lines`) and re-run it locally;
  `npm run test:ui` writes `.actual.png` / `.diff.png` into `shared/.artifacts/`. (red-ci-lanes)

- **Capturing a floating popup** — set `viewportOnly: true`: a full-page capture scrolls, and
  scrolling dismisses tips, legends and pops. (floating-popup-dies)

- **Waiting for a page to be ready** — wait on the observable state the pages settle into (the
  footer version popup's text, the search placeholder's show count; `case-helpers.js`) plus
  `document.fonts.ready`, never `networkidle`. (ready-networkidle)

- **Capturing hover-driven UI** — open it inside `capture()`, not `drive()`: the runner settles
  the scroll between them, and the scroll fires `mouseleave`. (hover-driven-ui)

- **Capturing right after a click or drag that reflows the layout** — park the pointer
  off-element (`page.mouse.move(0, 0)`) before capturing; left resting, it can land on the next
  element and open its own hover-tip over the shot, non-deterministically between machines.
  (leftover-pointer-hover-tip)

- **Asserting a CSS-transition-driven value** — sample every frame across a bounded window from
  the trigger to the transition's end (a `MutationObserver`/`requestAnimationFrame` loop), never
  one delayed sample gated on the state change; a loaded machine can still miss a single sample.
  (sample-transition-every-frame)

## The fixture freeze

- **Needing data for a case** — use `shared/fixtures/data/`, a frozen snapshot of the real
  committed data cast by the committed builder for state variety; never reach for `site/data/`.
  Every deviation from the source bytes is an `ADJUST` in the builder.

- **Re-running the builder** — it re-casts every golden, so run it only with the owner's
  approval and land builder, fixtures, goldens and gallery in one reviewed change.

- **Having invoked `build-fixtures.js` at all**, even against a scratch edit — it writes into
  `fixtures/data/` as it goes, so `git diff --stat` the whole fixtures dir before deciding there
  is nothing to revert. (build-fixtures-partial-drift)

## Golden approval

- **A golden that no longer matches** — show the owner the committed golden beside
  `shared/.artifacts/<case>.actual.png` and `.diff.png` through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, one
  per item, and say so in the PR body.

- **Landing an intended UI change** — spec edit (doc-first, red), then the implementation, then
  `npm run refresh:ui`, with the refreshed PNGs in the same diff.

### Skill: requirements-harness
